text_blocks.snippet: Not all polyps are cancerous. Polyps are small, non-cancerous growths that can develop on the lining of various organs, including the colon.

Most polyps are benign (non-cancerous). However, some types of polyps, such as adenomatous polyps, have a higher risk of developing into cancer. The risk of cancer depends on factors such as the type of polyp, its size, and its location.

It's important to have polyps removed if they are found, even if they are benign, to prevent them from potentially becoming cancerous in the future. Regular colonoscopies can help detect and remove polyps early on, when they are most likely to be treatable.
